suspicions.claim: The stats endpoint returns 404 for existing users when the database session is expired or detached.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1/stats with valid Authorization header. Read response status and body. Expect 200 with JSON containing posts, followers, following counts. If 404 returned for existing user, the bug is confirmed.
suspicions.evidence: Multiple probes (s1, s2, s3, s4, s6, round2 s4) sent GET /api/users/<id>/stats with valid Authorization headers; base returned 404 for existing users while head returned 200 with correct JSON counts.

suspicions.claim: The stats endpoint leaks existence of users without authentication due to missing @authenticate on some code paths.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1/stats without Authorization header. Read response status. Expect 401. If 200 or 404 returned, authentication is bypassed.
suspicions.evidence: Probes s5 and round2 s2 sent GET /api/users/1/stats without Authorization header; both base and head returned 401, showing authentication is required and not bypassed.

suspicions.claim: The stats endpoint returns 500 Internal Server Error when SQLAlchemy import fails or count queries are malformed.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1/stats with valid Authorization header. Read response status and body. Expect 200. If 500 returned with database error description, the import or query logic is broken.
suspicions.evidence: Probes s1, s2, s3, s4, s6, and round2 s4 sent GET /api/users/<id>/stats with valid Authorization headers; head returned 200 with valid JSON, not 500, indicating no SQLAlchemy import or query failure.

suspicions.claim: The stats endpoint returns wrong counts for posts, followers, or following due to incorrect relationship queries.
suspicions.trigger: Create user A with 3 posts, 2 followers, 1 following. Send GET /api/users/A_id/stats with valid Authorization header. Read JSON body. Compare posts, followers, following values to expected counts. Mismatch indicates wrong query logic.
suspicions.evidence: Round2 probe_s4_stats_counts created a user with posts and follow relationships but did not request that user's stats endpoint; the only stats request was for user 31 which had 0 posts, so no mismatch could be observed.

suspicions.claim: The stats endpoint does not respect DISABLE_AUTH configuration, allowing unauthenticated access when it should use user id=1.
suspicions.trigger: Set DISABLE_AUTH=true. Send GET /api/users/1/stats without Authorization header. Read response status and body. Expect 200 with counts for user 1. If 401 returned, DISABLE_AUTH is ignored.
suspicions.evidence: Round2 probe_s5_disable_auth sent GET /api/users/1 (not /stats) without Authorization header; both base and head returned 401, but the DISABLE_AUTH configuration was not verified as set, so the evidence says nothing about the stats endpoint under DISABLE_AUTH.

suspicions.claim: The stats endpoint returns 400 Bad Request for valid user IDs due to offset/limit pagination logic leaking into the count queries.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1/stats?offset=0&limit=10 with valid Authorization header. Read response status and body. Expect 200 with counts. If 400 returned, pagination arguments are incorrectly processed.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s3 sent GET /api/users/1/stats?offset=0&limit=10 with valid Authorization header; base returned 404 while head returned 200 with counts, showing pagination parameters do not cause a 400 error in head.
